title: Prime In Diagonal
summary: Given a 0-indexed two-dimensional integer array nums, identify the largest prime number that appears on any of its diagonals.
statement: Given a 0-indexed two-dimensional integer array nums, identify the largest prime number that appears on any of its diagonals. If no prime number is found on the diagonals, return 0. A prime number is defined as an integer greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself. An integer is considered to be on a diagonal if it is equal to nums[i][i] or nums[i][nums.length - i - 1] for some integer i.
constraints: nums is a nonempty square integer matrix.
Inspect both the main and anti-diagonal entries.
Return the largest prime found there, or zero when neither diagonal contains a prime.
hints: Only two cells per row can lie on the required diagonals.
Test primality by trial divisors only through the integer square root.
Update the maximum for both diagonal positions in every row.
A composite has a factor no larger than its square root, so the test is complete and every eligible matrix cell is inspected.
editorial: A composite has a factor no larger than its square root, so the test is complete and every eligible matrix cell is inspected.
